# Terminal Deck

> A desktop workspace for AI coding agents. It runs Claude Code, Codex CLI and
> Gemini CLI — or any agent you add by naming its command — as real terminal
> sessions in one window, with a tab and a live status dot per session, and the
> same sessions reachable from a phone or a browser. Free, MIT-licensed, no
> account, no telemetry, no analytics. macOS and Windows have a window; Linux
> runs the same core as a headless host with no Electron in it. Version 0.15.0.

This file is the repository's index. The site keeps a fuller one:
https://terminaldeck.dev/llms.txt is a short index of every page, and
https://terminaldeck.dev/llms-full.txt is every page as one markdown file.

## What it is

One window that runs coding agents as real processes on pseudo-terminals.
Nothing is reimplemented and nothing sits between you and the CLI: whatever
`claude`, `codex` or `gemini` does in your own terminal it does here, including
anything a version released after this app gains.

## The parts that are not obvious from a feature list

- The status dot is read off the SCREEN, not off the process. Each session's
  output is fed to a headless terminal emulator in the main process, and what
  that emulator has drawn is classified into working, waiting, needs-input or
  exited. It is therefore accurate for tabs nobody is looking at, and it
  survives a CLI repainting its own interface — which a process-state check
  cannot do, because a CLI waiting on a human and a CLI thinking look identical
  from outside.
- Token use, cache hit rate and context-window pressure are read out of Claude
  Code's own JSONL transcripts, not counted here and not asked for over an API.
- There is no dollar figure anywhere in the app, deliberately. A per-token price
  misleads somebody on a subscription and a subscription price cannot be
  computed from anything any provider publishes. A pricing display was built and
  then removed.
- The copilot — the assistant that works the app itself — is a real session in
  the same sandbox as any other, with routines that fire on an event (a session
  finishing, git state changing, a file changing) rather than on a clock.
- A phone reaches a desktop with no port forwarding, no VPN and nothing to set
  up on anybody's network: both ends dial out to a rendezvous server that
  staples the two sockets together and carries a Noise IK channel it holds no
  key for. It keeps no accounts and no database and maps a host name to a socket
  in memory only.
- The embedded browser can be driven by an agent through the browser's own
  debugging protocol and hands the page back the instant a human touches it.
  Clicking an element sends the agent a CSS selector rather than a description
  of what was clicked.
- Nothing here handles API keys or logins. It launches the CLI that is already
  installed and inherits whatever authentication that CLI already uses.
- A Kanban board was built and then deleted, code and all, because a board is a
  thing kept up to date by hand and nothing else in the app asks that. The QR
  code and the pairing link went the same way: pairing is six digits shown on
  the desktop and approved there.

## Where things are

- [README.md](README.md): what it is, what ships today, how to install it and
  how to build it from source.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): grouped by what changed rather than by commit
  order. Its Unreleased section is the honest answer to whether a tag contains
  a given feature.
- [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md): the build, the packaging and the release process.
- [HEADLESS.md](HEADLESS.md): the Linux/WSL host — plain Node, no Electron.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- `src/main/` the Electron main process, which owns every session and is the
  only part allowed to start a program or open a file.
- `src/renderer/` the window. It cannot reach a process or a file directly;
  everything goes through one narrow IPC surface.
- `src/shared/` the types and constants both halves agree on. The product name
  lives in `src/shared/brand.ts` and nowhere else.
- `host/` the headless host. `android/`, `ios/`, `pwa/` the clients.

## What is not built yet

Notarisation on macOS and a Windows signing certificate. Translations. Voice
dictation — the app cannot transcribe, so the microphone is off by default and
it hands over to the operating system's own dictation. An App Store release of
the iPhone client, which is on TestFlight, internal testing only. A Google Play
listing for the Android client, whose signed APK ships with every release but
cannot update itself without one. There is no Linux window. On macOS, Apple
silicon only; on Windows, x64 only.
